courses.text: Skip to content Home Courses Community Login Coming soon Start date: December 1, 2026 Blockchain Fundamentals 1 Free · 20 weeks Blockchain Fundamentals 1 is a free, 20-week program combining expert lectures, small-group research, and peer teaching across 10 topics. Join us online on Tuesdays, starting December 1, 2026. Application deadline: November 8, 2026 at 23:59. Acceptance announcements: November 22, 2026. Apply now Course information From digital trust and Bitcoin to smart contracts, DeFi, and crypto taxation: build your understanding one topic at a time. Course Description Curriculum FAQ Lecture weeks and presentation weeks alternate. An industry expert introduces a topic in a live lecture with Q&A. In small peer groups of three, you research one of four subtopics and prepare a 10–15-minute presentation. The following week, you teach your subtopic to other groups and learn from theirs — the jigsaw learning model. A new topic begins at the next lecture session. Sessions last 1.5 hours and take place online on Tuesdays. Teams rotate during the program so you can work with more peers. Use Moodle for materials and assignments, and Zoom for meetings; recordings and additional learning resources are provided. Cameras are required during sessions. For each presentation, create an original diagram, timeline, or comparison table, and use primary sources such as whitepapers and developer documentation. Set aside additional time outside sessions for research and preparation. Expand All Foundational Trust · Weeks 1–4 Weeks 1–2: Decentralization & Digital Trust Why decentralization matters, the double-spending problem, and shared ledgers. Weeks 3–4: Cryptography, Hashing, Keys & Signatures How hashes protect integrity, and how public/private keys and digital signatures establish identity. The Ledger Architecture · Weeks 5–8 Weeks 5–6: Wallets & Peer-to-Peer Networks Wallet types, key management, node roles, and how transactions and blocks travel across a network. Weeks 7–8: Bitcoin Data Structure & Transactions Block structure, the UTXO model, and the journey from signing a transaction to confirmation. Securing the State · Weeks 9–12 Weeks 9–10: Proof-of-Work, Proof-of-Stake & the Blockchain Trilemma Mining, validators, incentives, and the trade-offs between security, scalability, and decentralization. Weeks 11–12: Ethereum — The World Computer The move to programmable blockchains, accounts, application state, and the Ethereum Virtual Machine. The Programmable Layer · Weeks 13–16 Weeks 13–14: Smart Contracts, Gas, Token Standards & Oracles How smart contracts execute, why gas is needed, and how tokens and off-chain data fit into applications. Weeks 15–16: Tokenomics Token supply, market capitalization, fully diluted valuation, and metrics for understanding token economics. The New Economy · Weeks 17–20 Weeks 17–18: Stablecoins, Real World Assets & DeFi Stablecoin models, tokenized assets, decentralized exchanges, and lending and borrowing protocols. Weeks 19–20: Taxation in Crypto An introduction to crypto taxation and regulation, with practical examples and a focus on Germany. Who can join? Eligibility and prerequisites will be confirmed with the course details. How much time is required? The free, 20-week program starts on December 1, 2026. Join a 1.5-hour online session on Tuesdays, alternating lecture and presentation weeks. Allow additional time for group research and preparation; that workload is not yet specified. The exact start time and timezone are still to be confirmed. How do I apply? Apply through the application form . Applications run from October 12 to November 8, 2026 at 23:59. Acceptance announcements: November 22, 2026. The deadline timezone is still to be confirmed. What time are the sessions? Sessions take place on Tuesdays and last 1.5 hours. The planned start is between 5:00 and 5:30 PM; the exact time and timezone will be confirmed. The first session is December 1, 2026. Holiday-break dates and the final calendar will be shared separately. Will I receive a certificate? Eligible participants receive a PDF and NFT certificate after the cohort. Detailed participation and points requirements will be confirmed before the program begins. Previous speakers Speakers from previous cohorts. The upcoming cohort’s lineup will be announced separately. Dr. David An Partner @Dracoon Ventures Previous topic: "Proof of Work, Mining, and Immutability" Jonas Gebele Research Associate @Technical University of Munich Previous topic: "Cryptography and Hashing" David Kurz Business Development @Bitvavo Previous topic: "Ethereum: The World Computer (Architecture)" Hear From the Students “I joined the course with almost no prior knowledge of Web3, but the structure made it easy to follow. The sessions were beginner-friendly, and the community helped me feel more confident asking questions and exploring the topic further.” Course Participant, Cohort 1 “It was a good starting point if you're curious about blockchain but don't know where to begin. Some topics were challenging, but the structure made them manageable. Before joining, I had heard about Bitcoin, Ethereum, and DeFi, but I didn't really understand how they connected. The course helped me build a clearer mental map of the Web3 ecosystem.” Course Participant, Cohort 2 “I joined the course with almost no prior knowledge of Web3, but the structure made it easy to follow. The sessions were beginner-friendly, and the community helped me feel more confident asking questions and exploring the topic further.” Course Participant, Cohort 1 “I joined the course with almost no prior knowledge of Web3, but the structure made it easy to follow. The sessions were beginner-friendly, and the community helped me feel more confident asking questions and exploring the topic further.” Course Participant, Cohort 1 “I liked that the course didn't assume everyone already knew the terminology. It started with the basics and then slowly connected the topics, which made the more technical parts easier to understand.” Course Participant, Cohort 1 “I joined the course with almost no prior knowledge of Web3, but the structure made it easy to follow. The sessions were beginner-friendly, and the community helped me feel more confident asking questions and exploring the topic further.” Course Participant, Cohort 1 “The group research format was useful because it made me go deeper into one topic instead of only listening passively. Presenting it to others also helped me understand where I still had gaps.” Course Participant, Cohort 3 “I joined the course with almost no prior knowledge of Web3, but the structure made it easy to follow. The sessions were beginner-friendly, and the community helped me feel more confident asking questions and exploring the topic further.” Course Participant, Cohort 1 Learn. Connect. Explore Web3.
